issue_context.title: Insert zero date successfully in default sql mode
issue_context.body:
## Bug Report

Please answer these questions before submitting your issue. Thanks!

1. What did you do?
If possible, provide a recipe for reproducing the error.
```
create table t(a date);
insert into t values('0000-00-0');
```

Relate issue: #8637

2. What did you expect to see?
```
mysql> create table t(a date);
Query OK, 0 rows affected (0.07 sec)

mysql> insert into t values('0000-00-0');
ERROR 1292 (22007): Incorrect date value: '0000-00-0' for column 'a' at row 1
```



3. What did you see instead?
```
mysql> create table t(a date);
Query OK, 0 rows affected (0.01 sec)

mysql> insert into t values('0000-00-0');
Query OK, 1 row affected (0.00 sec)

mysql> select * from t;
+------------+
| a          |
+------------+
| 0000-00-00 |
+------------+
1 row in set (0.00 sec)
```



4. What version of TiDB are you using (`tidb-server -V` or run `select tidb_version();` on TiDB)?
master
comments: Thanks for your report, @wjhuang2016 ! Would you want to fix it?

> Thanks for your report, @wjhuang2016 ! Would you want to fix it?

Yeah, I will try to fix it.

review_comments:
If we want to insert N rows, is the complexity of this operation for this SQL `O(N*N)`?
And why do we have to do a converting?
How about letting the underlying expression return error `ErrWarnDataOutOfRange` directly?

Return `ErrWarnDataOutOfRange` directly is not compatible with MySQL.
As MySQL return `Out of range value for column 'a' at row 1`,
but we return `constant -1 overflows bigint`,
PR([#9829](https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/pull/9829)) does not fix this problem. 

Another way to do this is modify `func (sc *StatementContext) HandleTruncate(err error) error`,
delete `TruncateAsWarning`, and do this in upper function, but this will introduce some repetitive code.
